lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: why all circles are similar

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle intercepts a 100° arc. Find it.

steps: Inscribed angle is half the arc.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3. From an external point 5 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 2, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
4, because the tangent bisects the radius
8, because the tangent extends beyond the circle

items.prompt: A circle has radius 9. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 60°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 34°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 104°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 7. From an external point 25 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 18, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
24, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
24, because the tangent bisects the radius
32, because the tangent extends beyond the circle

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 8. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 45°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 81°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
